limitations: Detection is lexical, static, and inferred. It does not prove reachability, initialization, runtime coverage, effect, vulnerability, or enforcement, and it emits no observed basis or behavioral verdict.

The closed source parser covers JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python extensions only. Recognized other source extensions produce one explicit unsupported-language uncertainty; generic runtime-registration uncertainty remains even when an extension is not classified.

JavaScript slash expressions, template interpolation, Python formatted strings, malformed import syntax, dynamic names, and unknown HTTP method receivers are not evaluated; they are conservatively skipped with an explicit uncertainty.

Package JSON discovery is limited to dependency sections and main/module/bin entrypoints. Requirements parsing only extracts a leading package-like name and does not validate or resolve requirement syntax. Other selected manifests remain opaque.

Call-name classification can produce lexical false positives. Confidence is inferred/medium and later graph normalization must preserve provenance and uncertainty rather than upgrade it to observed behavior.

The selected Mastra scan qualifies only passive source evidence for the MVP clone. SDK descriptor compatibility, expected coverage, CLI model emission, and no-network/no-source-change acceptance remain later Phase 02 tasks.
